newsitem.title: RUSSIA: FOCUS-Russia Eurobond in March may be 2 bln marks.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Russia Eurobond in March may be 2 bln marks.

text.p: Russia will return to the Eurobond market next month with a jumbo issue for as much as two billion marks ($1.2 billion), a senior Deutsche Bank official said on Friday.

Georg Krupp, the Deutsche board member responsible for Russia, told a news conference that paperwork on rescheduling $32 billion of former Soviet debt to Western banks was taking longer than expected but would be over in a few months.

And in a further sign of Russia's growing creditworthiness, he said Germany's biggest bank had agreed to lend Russia's Gazprom gas monopoly 1.5 billion marks to finance a new pipeline to Western Europe.
Krupp said he had discussed the Eurobond with Finance Minister Alexander Livshits on Thursday.
"He again confirmed, and we agreed, that Deutsche Bank has received the mandate to issue the first mark Eurobond for the Russian Federation with a volume of 1.5 to 2.0 billion marks," Krupp said.
"We assume that we can go to market with the bond at the end of next week," he added, saying Russia would hold investor presentations on the bond in Frankfurt and Zurich next week.

Later Deutsche's investment banking division Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, which is joint lead manager of the bond, said the presentations would be held in the week beginning March 10, with the Eurobond likely to be issued at the end of the week.
Russia's debut $1 billion Eurobond last November marked its first return as a sovereign borrower to international capital markets since the Bolshevik revolution. The issue was heavily oversubscribed.
It was the biggest ever debut sovereign Eurobond and strong demand from Western investors enabled Russia to raise two or three times more than originally planned.

Demand is welling up for the mark offering, too -- Russian officials had been earlier talking of one or 1.5 billion marks. "The way market conditions are now, we can issue a bond of up to two billion marks," Krupp said.
He said the rescheduling of Soviet commercial bank debt assumed by Russia was almost complete.

Under the deal agreed last November, the banks have rescheduled repayment of $24 billion of principal over up to 25 years and $8 billion of interest arrears over 20 years, with seven years' grace in both cases.
But closing the deal is being delayed by detailed work of reconciling 30,000 individual loans with their rightful creditors.
"The process is running now at high speed. It will take a little more time. We hope that it can be completed in the next two to three months," Krupp said.
Delays by the International Monetary Fund in paying out instalments of its $10 billion loan to Russia would not affect the final closure of the bank debt rescheduling, he said.

Deutsche's confidence in the Russian market was underlined by an agreement to lend 1.5 billion marks for up to 10 years to Gazprom, which is building a new pipeline from the Yamal gas field to Western Europe, Krupp said.
The credit is in addition to a $2.5 billion syndicated loan led by Dresdner Bank, signed in Frankfurt on Friday, to fund the same project. ($ = 1.691 German Marks)
